concepts.description: The full Flower composer discovers working-directory files and directories through @, keeps editable chips in connection memory, and admits exact ordered references to Floret.

frontmatter.description: The full Flower composer discovers working-directory files and directories through @, keeps editable chips in connection memory, and admits exact ordered references to Floret.
frontmatter.title: Flower composer references

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Redeven owns reference discovery and unadmitted draft editing; Floret is the sole canonical source after admission.
- Outcome: a whitespace-boundary `@` token selects one working-directory file or directory as an ordered reference chip without adding prompt text or file content.
- Invariants: discovery uses the host's authorized filesystem adapter, all visible placements in one connection share one in-memory scope, and one strict `flower_composer` context action preserves the frozen order and directory kind.
- Failure boundary: stale search generations, malformed wire data, or admission mismatches fail without discarding the connection-local editor, creating a different queued command, or writing canonical Floret state.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Composer interaction

The full composer recognizes an editable `@` token only at a whitespace boundary with a collapsed caret. IME composition and range selections suppress discovery. Selecting a candidate removes the complete token, preserves surrounding Unicode text and spacing, and adds a separate file or directory chip; the removed token is not sent as prompt text. Selecting an existing reference does not duplicate it. Chip removal restores focus predictably, and add and remove mutate the exact connection-local composer scope synchronously. Activity, Workbench, and retained companion placements observe the same scope without an editor lease, takeover, conflict state, or persistence recovery path.

The combobox keeps focus in the textarea while Arrow keys move one stable active candidate, Enter or Tab selects it, and Escape dismisses the current token result. Pointer selection, retry, loading, empty, and error states use the same active identity and ARIA listbox contract. The composer announces add, duplicate, and removal outcomes through a polite live region. Reference chips remain separate from attachment previews. In the bottom command row the attachment button is fixed immediately before the More overflow control, while compact context controls retain their existing overflow behavior.

## Bounded discovery

Discovery searches the current thread's immutable working directory or the new-thread working-directory draft. `FlowerSurfaceAdapter.listWorkingDirectoryEntries` is the only search capability: Env App and Desktop implement it through their existing authenticated runtime filesystem bridges. The shared UI does not read a local path directly.

The index bounds recursion depth, listed directories, entries per directory, total candidates, path length, visible results, and cache lifetime. It skips generated and dependency directories, stays within the normalized root, and ranks exact name, name prefix, name substring, then relative-path fuzzy matches with deterministic depth/path tie breaking. Runtime/root cache identity and monotonically changing search generations prevent a late or aborted scan from replacing a newer query. Root read errors are visible and retryable; inaccessible descendants are skipped within the same bounded scan.

## Draft and admission

The connection-local composer stores ordered file/directory chips with a product-local identity, host-derived label, and opaque normalized path. It is never written to Redeven, Floret, local storage, IndexedDB, or another connection. The first-release product v1 baseline has no server draft, draft migration, or compatibility reader; [Flower storage ownership and migrations](../ai/flower-storage-ownership-and-migrations.md) defines that boundary.

Send freezes the ordered references with the text, attachments, model, and stable product request identity. It creates one strict Ask Flower action whose source surface is `flower_composer`; each context item contains exactly `kind=file_path`, `path`, and `is_directory`. Unknown envelope, target, source, presentation, execution-context, or item fields are invalid. The action never accepts a client-authored root, display label, TurnID, or RunID. Prepare, direct admission, queued creation, and queued replacement carry the same normalized JSON.

The host freezes the editor value and strict context action under the exact `client_request_id` or `queue_id` before admission. Path, order, directory bit, action source, or JSON changes under the same product identity reject the attempt without replacing the accepted command. After admission, the one-pass mapping defined by [AI tool runtime](../ai/ai-tool-runtime.md) gives Floret the canonical ordered `MessageReference` values and current-turn supplemental context.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Search results and persisted paths are display and navigation metadata, not filesystem authorization. Discovery observes only what the current authorized host adapter returns under the current runtime and working directory. A reference does not read or attach file contents, grant future filesystem access, or substitute for an explicit attachment upload.

Before Send, Redeven does not persist the ordered editable reference snapshot. After Send, Redeven may retain the immutable unadmitted command and its strict ordered action for retry and settlement; the product-local chip identity and label are not canonical identity or admission authority. Once admitted, Redeven does not retain a second queryable message-reference record, and canonical reference presentation and navigation derive from Floret reads plus current host authorization.

concepts.summary: Flower is a reusable presentation surface over Floret-owned conversation and execution state. This overview is the canonical navigation point for timeline ordering, model/navigation behavior, terminal activity, approval/context state, and subagent detail. The focused concepts own their independent UI contracts so search and open operations can retrieve one behavior without loading the complete Flower implementation history.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism

This concept is the stable overview for the subject. Detailed contracts are maintained in the focused concepts below:

- [Flower timeline ordering](flower-timeline-ordering.md)
- [Flower model and navigation presentation](flower-model-navigation.md)
- [Flower terminal activity presentation](flower-terminal-activity.md)
- [Flower approval and context state](flower-approval-context.md)
- [Flower subagent detail presentation](flower-subagent-detail.md)

The focused timeline contract preserves Floret `ThroughOrdinal` and `ListThreadTurns` ordering, maps a valid non-renderable turn to `turn_projection_unavailable`, and records rejected public contracts as `floret.contract.rejected`; the detailed rules live in [Flower timeline ordering](flower-timeline-ordering.md).

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower must not reconstruct canonical execution, approval, context, read, or child state from transcript text, audit rows, previews, timestamps, or local heuristics. Full timeline replacement is reserved for explicit resynchronization, snapshot recovery, and terminal settlement finalization.

Realtime observation uses the Redeven Flower live hub and a single fetch-SSE connection per authorized surface. The hub performs canonical projection, privacy sanitization, deduplication, coalescing, and JSON encoding once, then fans out immutable batches to independent observer queues. Summary and selected-thread cursors carry explicit stream generations; a retention gap, generation reset, service restart, or slow-observer overflow emits one `resync_required` envelope and closes that observer. Flower keeps full detail for eight recent threads, retains all summary rows, and reboots an evicted selection from canonical bootstrap without clearing its separate composer or attachment state. Canonical batches exclude private read state; `viewer.read_state` is delivered only to connections for the same user. Hidden pages cancel their reader, and healthy heartbeats do not create application polling requests.

frontmatter.title: Flower model and navigation presentation

concepts.summary: Flower keeps environment and Desktop model sources explicit, preserves thread-owned model and reasoning defaults, and presents unavailable selections without replacing the ordinary conversation layout. Thread selection separates immediate visual intent from committed content and rejects stale loads. Transient operation failures use host notifications instead of transcript content, while canonical run and tool failures stay with their owning timeline renderers.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism

The shared Flower settings contract separates `defaults.permission_type`, nullable `model_profile`, and optional `model_source`. Its adapter exposes independent `saveDefaultPermission`, `saveModelProfile`, and `persistDefaultModel` operations. The permission control is always present and uses a 700 ms serialized autosave controller that coalesces rapid changes, never allows response order to overwrite a newer choice, and restores the last confirmed value after failure. An absent environment profile is a neutral setup state rather than a global Flower error. A `remote_desktop` Env App session may expose the Desktop model catalog alongside the environment profile in the same snapshot; `local_host` and ordinary browser sessions ignore the unbound Desktop diagnostic object. The settings surface always edits the environment provider profile. Desktop source status never replaces the provider editor with a managed-source panel, and Desktop model selection belongs in the composer menu.

Thread snapshots, list items, and thread patches carry `model_id` and `reasoning_selection` as thread defaults. Flower renders a fused model/reasoning segmented control in the composer when model options are available; the reasoning segment is shown only when the selected model exposes controllable reasoning capability. A ready Desktop model source contributes a read-only model catalog alongside editable environment provider models, preserving each opaque model id, display label, token limits, modalities, and reasoning capability. Every composer option has an explicit source: `model_profile`, `desktop_model_source`, or `thread_snapshot`. `thread_snapshot` is a disabled, ungrouped option used only when an existing thread references a model no longer present in either catalog; Flower does not regroup or silently replace that model. When both active catalogs exist, the compact menu groups the environment models first under the environment display name and Desktop models second under the fixed `Desktop` name; a single active source remains a flat list. A new Flower mount selects the environment profile's persisted `current_model_id`, falling back to the Desktop current model only when the environment profile is absent. Selecting another environment model calls `persistDefaultModel`; selecting a Desktop model writes only the mounted surface's pending-new-thread draft. Repeated New Chat actions in that mount retain the draft, while a remount restores the environment default. Creating a new thread always sends the chosen draft model explicitly, and draft reasoning is included only when that model supports reasoning control. Switching to a model without reasoning removes any draft reasoning override before launch. An existing thread always resolves its own `model_id` first. Changing it sends `setThreadModel`; an environment-model change then persists the environment default, while a Desktop-model change stops after the thread PATCH. Returning to New Chat restores the mount's pending-new-thread choice without copying the thread model into the environment default. Readiness is evaluated for the selected option's source: environment models require their provider and web-search keys, while Desktop models require a `ready` source containing that exact model id. If the selected model is unavailable but another source is usable, the composer and model menu remain visible, send stays disabled, the model trigger shows a compact warning, and the menu shows one compact Desktop status row without a global banner. If no model from either source is usable, Flower keeps the ordinary empty state and renders one single-line composer status row with warning, refresh, and one owner-specific action; it does not render a transcript-sized setup guide. Refresh calls only `adapter.loadSettings()` and atomically replaces the settings snapshot, preserving thread selection, input, attachments, mounted Desktop draft, and environment default. `missing_keys` and `empty` recover through local Flower settings, `unsupported` through remote Runtime settings, and `unbound`, `connecting`, `expired`, or `error` through Desktop Connection Center. Existing-thread launch does not add a global model override, so subsequent turns use the persisted thread default unless the request is intentionally local to a waiting-input response. The model/reasoning segmented control is disabled while the selected thread is active, waiting for user input, compacting, read-only, or otherwise unable to accept a thread preference change. The Flower UI quality gate explicitly runs a cross-layer Desktop model-source test that renders the shared surface over the real Env adapter and verifies catalog projection, labels, reasoning defaults, thread creation, and first-turn RPC payloads together.

Flower treats user-triggered operation failures and input blockers as transient feedback, not transcript content. The shared surface emits a host notification intent for send failures, invalid or blocked submits, model/default-model persistence failures, permission changes, approval submits, and sidebar actions; Env App and Desktop render that intent as a toast through their own notification systems. These toasts do not change the canonical thread timeline, and Flower no longer inserts composer or sidebar error cards into the page flow for those transient actions. Run failures, tool failures, subagent detail errors, and other structured timeline/detail content remain rendered by their owning timeline or detail renderer rather than being guessed from the notification channel.

Thread navigation separates visual, requested, and displayed ownership. A user click marks the list row immediately, then commits selection after the intent paint. A thread whose detail is already in the explicit warm set is displayed atomically without calling `loadThread` again. A cold target loads in staging while the previous transcript remains visible and read-only; only the newest request may publish the target transcript, focus the composer, restore tail position, or emit `content_presented`. Compose mode, permission changes, programmatic focus ownership, and newer thread requests cancel or supersede the pending user transaction. Codex uses the same product contract with separate selected, foreground, displayed, loading, and session-cache state, so warm sessions switch without provider or transcript remount and stale loads cannot replace the current thread.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower does not treat the global current model as an implicit existing-thread launch override. The current model is the default for the next newly created thread only. After a thread exists, its `model_id` and `reasoning_selection` are the displayed defaults; composer model changes write through to `current_model_id` only as a future new-thread default and never as a reverse sync into existing threads.

The Activity companion reuses this model and selection contract; its placement, presence, read gate, and Activity/Workbench focus isolation are defined in [Flower Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md). The header switcher is only a product-specific compact presentation; it does not create a second selected-thread owner or change the requested, committed, and content-presented ordering.

frontmatter.title: Flower subagent detail presentation

concepts.summary:
- Authority: Floret `ListSubAgents` owns child membership and `ReadSubAgentDetail` owns child execution detail.
- Outcome: Flower opens a parent-scoped, read-only child ledger without navigating to or creating a Redeven child thread.
- Invariants: every public child route uses canonical `thread_id`; `task_name` is required and never guessed from title, role, description, or message.
- Failure boundary: malformed summaries, missing canonical identity, parent-child mismatch, or invalid detail contracts are rejected rather than mapped through legacy aliases.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
Thread-level child membership comes from Floret through the active parent host or provider-free maintenance host. Redeven maps that snapshot into `thread.subagents` for bootstrap and live patches. Thread list refreshes that omit the field preserve selected-thread detail; only an explicit authoritative value replaces it. The header dropdown never scans transcript activity, audit rows, or child settings.

`FlowerSubagentSummary` contains `parent_thread_id`, canonical child `thread_id`, required `task_name`, task description, agent type, context mode, status, timing, and current control flags. There is no `subagent_id` or `title` compatibility field. Activity payloads route `Open messages` with `thread_id` only. Delegated approval presentation uses `child_thread_id`; it does not duplicate the same identity under another name.

The dropdown is a compact accessible floating surface over the parent thread. Active and ended groups stay visible, rows sort by canonical status and update time, and keyboard navigation supports arrows, Home, End, Enter, and Escape. Selecting a row opens the parent-scoped detail API in a read-only floating window. It does not select a sidebar child thread or create a child composer.

The detail window maps Floret's unified `ThreadDetailEvent` values and canonical child Activity timeline into the shared message/activity renderers. It supports pagination, active tailing, request identity guards, bottom-follow behavior, local retry, and disclosure-preserving operation groups. Preview rows remain inspection data and are not treated as complete output when Floret marks them as bounded. The detail ledger is human UI state and is not injected into the parent model context.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: Flower must not recover a missing child identity from activity sidecars, a title, a delegated approval alias, a fallback thread id, or local state. It must not humanize an absent task name into a role-based label. Redeven does not read Floret storage tables, persist child membership, create child `ThreadSettings`, or use detail events as a second transcript authority.

frontmatter.title: Flower terminal activity presentation

concepts.summary: Terminal activity is a renderer-first view over canonical Floret Activity items, not a second process lifecycle. Redeven maps display data only from Floret v3 `ActivityItem.presentation`, so the compact row shows `Shell` and the authored command instead of a protocol name. Approval state remains available to the actionable composer and lifecycle logic but never becomes ordinary activity presentation. Stable activity identity preserves user disclosure and viewport state across live replacements. Terminal output may poll Redeven process handles, but canonical status and completion remain projection-owned. Measured disclosure, local scrolling, transcript following, and reduced-motion handling preserve reading intent.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism

Terminal process activity remains part of that canonical projection. The Floret v3 wire contract keeps `label`, `description`, `renderer`, `chips`, `target_refs`, and `payload` under `ActivityItem.presentation`; identity, lifecycle, approval, and metadata remain on the item itself. Redeven accepts only non-empty presentation values from that nested shape and maps it consistently from bootstrap, block replacement, and timeline replacement. It tolerates but never reads null top-level placeholders emitted by the service JSON boundary, while any non-null legacy top-level presentation value fails closed. An item may temporarily omit presentation while a later canonical replacement enriches the same stable identity. A terminal row receives its command, status, process id, cumulative retained snapshot, and sequence facts from the Floret `ActivityTimeline` presentation produced by Redeven tool metadata. Its compact trigger always renders `Shell` plus the real `payload.command`; no terminal lifecycle may fall back to `terminal.exec`. `terminal.exec` publishes the process id as soon as the PTY starts through Floret's running activity update path, so `yield_ms` affects only when the agent receives the tool result, not when the user can inspect command progress. `terminal.read` and `terminal.terminate` retain their required user-language descriptions as secondary context while the same real command remains visible in the compact row and expanded command detail. Each read remains a separate activity row and its expanded panel shows only that call's `output` delta: a first read can show phase 1 and the next read can show phase 2 without making the command appear to have executed again. The public payload must not expose host-local path or input fields such as `cwd`, `workdir`, or `stdin`.

Expanded terminal rows are read-only product presentation. Completed status, output, exit code, and duration come directly from the canonical Floret Activity payload and never call a Redeven completion-output endpoint. Historical completed payloads that contain canonical output but predate sequence metadata render that output as an unsequenced static snapshot; only replacement accepts this `first_seq=last_seq=0` form, while live deltas remain sequence-strict. The shared terminal store applies two explicit sequence operations while the Activity remains running: a newer exec snapshot replaces the cumulative view, while a contiguous PTY process-read delta appends to it. Equal or older snapshots are ignored by sequence, an empty delta does not clear existing exec output, and an explicit `truncated=true` gap replaces the unavailable prefix with the retained delta. The store never decides cumulative-versus-incremental behavior with string prefix or substring checks. Flower and Env App send only the required `after_seq` process-read query for a running Activity with a public process id; server-owned waits and page limits are not UI options. Polling may continue while details are collapsed so a stored delta is not lost merely because it was not visible when it arrived. A valid process read can return a terminal `success`, `error`, or `canceled` snapshot when the PTY finishes between polls, including an empty delta whose `last_seq` remains equal to `after_seq`; that response stops local polling but can never change canonical Activity status, create lifecycle facts, or trigger settlement. Raw AppServer errors are logged for diagnostics and render only localized live-output or terminal-action failure text. The surface exposes icon-only actions to reveal and copy the full raw command and caps output at five visual line boxes using explicit font size, line height, padding, and border-box sizing; shorter output uses its natural height, while later lines increase only the local scroll height. Every pending terminal process binds its complete Floret settlement target and creating top-level or subagent Host before launch. After the pending handle is exposed and PTY reap completes, one finalizer performs one settlement through that owner; process reads, writes, cleanup, and later UI access never trigger or retry settlement, and no maintenance Host fallback exists. A ready settlement projection advances the same `ThroughOrdinal` cursor as every other projection and publishes the canonical `timeline.replaced` snapshot. An unavailable settlement projection remains committed Floret state, produces diagnostic logging, and is not read back or synthesized locally. `terminal.terminate` waits for process-tree exit, output drain, and finalization before returning, while `Service.Close` completes finalizers before releasing Floret Hosts and stores. Consequently, canonical terminal ordering and completion facts come only from durable Floret projections rather than a terminal-specific database, retry path, floor, refresh, or UI repair mechanism.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower activity details are renderer-first product views, not generic payload inspectors. `error`, `terminal`, `file`, `patch`, `web_search`, `question`, `completion`, `todos`, and `subagents` each have an explicit display model that prioritizes the information a normal user is trying to inspect: failure reason, terminal output, file content, diffs, search results, prompts and choices, outcomes, todo lists, or delegated task status. Read, list, find, grep, glob, and web operations expose only semantic scalar values or bounded scalar lists such as path, root, query, pattern, URL, and count. Unknown tools use a neutral `Called <semantic label>` title and the same safe scalar allowlist; a human label does not authorize rendering nested `data`, `result`, or arbitrary protocol JSON. Failed tools render the public error summary in the compact row and keep the complete public message in a collapsed error detail without exposing error codes, retryability flags, item ids, tool ids, or lifecycle diagnostics. Successful tools do not show generic completion summaries or event-code details such as `tool execution completed`, `todos.updated`, `file.updated`, `success`, `completed`, or `ok`. Rich structured metadata remains available only for explicitly designed product renderers such as OKF and skill activation.

Flower activity disclosure is presentation state over the canonical activity lifecycle, not a second execution state machine. Every stateful activity view uses one semantic identity composed from thread, run, turn, and canonical `item_id`; status, payload, message block position, item position, and renderer object identity are not part of that identity. `timeline.replaced` may move an activity between message blocks, but it must reuse the same activity row, disclosure controller, detail component, and terminal viewport. A live projection may first expose the stable item without a renderer or detail payload and later enrich that same item; the row keeps its DOM identity, while the disclosure trigger remains bound and its native disabled state follows detail availability. All pending, running, waiting, completed, and failed activity details remain closed until the user explicitly opens them. A manual expand or collapse persists across later lifecycle and canonical replacement updates for that stable item. Running terminal detail remains available on demand, but background progress never mounts detail or changes transcript geometry merely because time passed. Opening uses a 360 ms measured-height animation and closing uses a 300 ms animation. Approval state is not a row badge, chip, metadata line, title suffix, tooltip, expanded detail, or ordinary activity ARIA label. When an approval is actionable, the composer exclusively owns its approve and reject controls; completing a decision removes that dock without adding `approved` or any other approval outcome to history.

Open activity detail owns its real pixel height. A shared disclosure motion controller mounts at `0px`, measures the nearest detail content from its bounding rectangle, and uses the Chromium `ResizeObserver` and Web Animations APIs as required platform capabilities. Opening, resizing, retargeting, reversal, and closing are all owned by one current animation; its `finished` promise is the only completion signal that may advance presence state or unmount content. CSS does not own a second height-transition clock, and animation completion is not inferred from elapsed timers. Consecutive content changes cancel the previous animation and redirect the current visual height to the latest measured target. Content growth and shrinkage use a 280 ms animation, including terminal polling, command expansion, responsive reflow, error replacement, and disappearing controls. The nearest detail disclosure owns this dynamic resize; the Env App timeline wrapper animates only its own open or close, preventing nested height animations from compounding movement. Detail content remains capped at `min(42rem, 72vh)`, and terminal output remains capped at five visual lines; growth beyond those limits becomes local scrolling instead of continuing to move the conversation.

Flower schedules its existing transcript-tail follower on every disclosure animation frame. It preserves the bottom anchor only while the user is already following latest content, and it never forces a conversation back to the end after the user scrolls upward. Env App continues to use `VirtualMessageList` row `ResizeObserver` handling: following mode applies each intermediate height delta, while paused mode restores the captured viewport anchor after every observed height. Terminal panels use a separate local 24 px near-bottom threshold. Binding or reopening a terminal viewport begins a new local viewing session at the latest line. Each output update receives one presentation frame: following mode scrolls to the bottom before reporting the output as presented, while paused mode preserves `scrollTop` and still reports presentation completion. Upward wheel or scroll pauses local following, returning to the bottom resumes it, and canonical activity replacement does not reset that choice. Reduced-motion presentation commits measured pixel height without animation and unmounts closed detail immediately. Running and waiting rows use only transform, opacity, or color animation; no infinite animation may change `left`, width, height, or another geometric layout property. Closed detail is not mounted, and mounted detail uses `content-visibility` containment. These presentation rules do not alter Floret activity status, event ordering, persistence, read state, audit state, or terminal settlement.

concepts.summary: Flower renders server-ordered Floret turn pages and validated live projections without client-side message sorting or reconstruction. Durable ordinal order, projection availability, draft identity, decorations, and replacement events remain explicit contracts. Live drafts carry independent message-row and Turn identities and may update only the matching canonical thread, turn, and run; resynchronization replaces the timeline rather than inventing assistant content or recovering from product audit rows.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism

The Flower live bootstrap includes `timeline_messages` as the only ordered message source for a thread snapshot. Redeven obtains before/after/tail pages from Floret `ListThreadTurns` and preserves their ascending canonical ordinal order. Each `ThreadTurnSnapshot` maps to the Floret `UserEntryID` user row followed by that same turn's validated assistant projection or one anchored `turn_projection_unavailable` decoration. Every root timeline row carries its owning `turn_id`; the user row keeps `UserEntryID` as `message.id`, while user and assistant rows share the exact canonical TurnID and retain their real row/message ids. Missing or inconsistent TurnID makes the whole canonical projection fail instead of being inferred from a row id, prompt, timestamp, or position. Tool display details come from the projection `ActivityTimeline` plus Redeven's `ToolPresentationSpec`. A live draft may replace only the assistant slot whose `ThreadID`, `TurnID`, and `RunID` exactly match the canonical turn; terminal projection removes it. Redeven stores no transcript, TurnID-to-UserEntryID correlation row, run record, projection cache, preview, or ordering copy.

Projection application is strict and monotonic. Floret `ThreadTurnProjection.Validate()` owns identity completeness, finite status and segment kinds, positive durable `ThroughOrdinal`, activity timeline validity, and control-signal structure. Redeven checks only that the validated projection belongs to the current Flower run/thread/turn, then maps assistant text, activity timelines with Redeven file actions, and non-body control segments. Live projections accept `running`; history assembly separately requires `Status.IsTerminal()`. Redeven keeps the last applied ordinal for each full execution identity, ignores equal or older projections, and advances the cursor only after the complete projection maps and replaces the assistant blocks. A valid zero-segment projection clears the in-memory assistant block list without synthesizing an empty markdown block. Runtime stream envelopes carry `turn_id` independently from `message_id`; `message.started` must provide both before the reducer creates an assistant row, and subsequent block events update only that real message id. Runtime events are accepted only after Floret `runtime.Event.Validate()` validates their public event type and nested stream, activity, and projection data. Invalid contracts record `floret.contract.rejected` and leave the current presentation unchanged; private harness events never enter the public runtime sink.

Flower materializes lifecycle only from Floret bootstrap and live lifecycle fields. A complete canonical assistant message does not imply a successful terminal run: when assistant commit and terminal settlement arrive separately, Flower retains the Floret-projected running or terminal status until `thread_patch`, `live_state`, or `run.status_changed` supplies the authoritative transition. Local command pending state, accepted input-response receipts, SSE connectivity, visibility, selection, and detail-cache membership never synthesize running, success, failure, cancellation, or another canonical assistant. Pending submission previews, composer busy state, input-response handoff, and deferred stop remain local interaction state without changing the projected thread status.

Published Floret v3.2.33 includes the complete projection, structured attachments, and ordered `UserReferences` in each admitted public turn snapshot. The identity-bound overview reader returns canonical thread state and the latest admitted turn from the same active path, excluding marker-only turns until their user entry is committed. Floret validators own availability combinations, identity, status, through ordinal, attachments, references, control signals, approvals, and settlement agreement. Supported interrupted approval history is normalized by Floret's canonical projection from durable terminal turn authority; Redeven does not repair it. Redeven projects canonical attachment metadata into supported Flower blocks and maps references to a browser-safe DTO that omits opaque `ResourceRef`. Reference-only user messages remain visible, and admitted messages never recover linked context from the old queued `context_action`. An invalid snapshot or projection is a canonical consistency error and requests resynchronization; Redeven does not turn it into display content. Only a valid projection with no renderable assistant blocks maps to one `turn_projection_unavailable` decoration with reason `not_renderable` immediately after that turn's user row. Flower renders “Response unavailable” with no retry control and no invented assistant body. Storage, I/O, pagination, unknown row cursors, and same-revision thread consistency failures remain request errors rather than being downgraded. Bootstrap, paged history, and `timeline.replaced` never recover content from metadata, product run errors, audit records, previews, or stale live drafts.

Floret v3.2.33 also preserves sanitized host presentation for a parseable schema-invalid tool call while rejecting its execution. Flower therefore renders the attempted command or other mapped call label from canonical Activity instead of a generic tool identifier. Redeven does not parse provider arguments from projection metadata or add a renderer fallback; malformed JSON remains presentation-free and no invalid call reaches permission or side-effect handling.

The same canonical projection preserves an existing tool presentation while approval lifecycle details advance that item's waiting or pending state. Approval request and resolution cannot replace a terminal command label, renderer, description, or payload with generic approval presentation; approval-only history may use Floret's neutral fallback. Redeven maps the published projection directly and does not display an approval status row.

Timeline decorations are a strict discriminated union. `context_compaction` owns only a compaction payload, while `turn_projection_unavailable` owns only its projection-unavailable payload and finite reason. Unknown kinds, missing payloads, mixed payloads, invalid reason codes, or missing message anchors fail mapping explicitly. `ListThreadMessagesResponse`, live bootstrap, and full replacement snapshots carry `timeline_decorations` beside the messages produced by the same timeline projection, so a valid assistant projection and an unavailable decoration are mutually exclusive for one turn.

Live streaming uses server events only for current-process presentation. `message.started` may create one assistant streaming row only when thread, TurnID, RunID, and MessageID are all nonempty; those identities may be distinct and become immutable for that draft in both server and browser materializers. Every later block-start, delta, block-set, or failure event must find that exact existing draft and match all four identities. An activity block delivered by `message.block_set` must also carry the same thread, turn, and run as the event envelope before it may replace a block. A missing draft or mismatched identity requests resynchronization and never synthesizes, repairs, or retargets a message. Reconnect continues from the materialized exact draft. There is no realtime transcript-message or transcript-reset event, and user messages are never inserted through the live stream. Floret text deltas may render temporary live markdown, while a validated `runtime.Event.Projection` with status `running` replaces only the matching live assistant draft with current assistant text and activity blocks. Aggregate Floret `runtime.Event.ActivityTimeline` remains lifecycle observation data and does not create main-thread activity blocks by itself. A local tool row is pending when Floret has observed the model's tool call but has not dispatched the handler; it becomes running only from Floret's dispatch-start lifecycle fact after permission and approval gates pass. Batched ordinary calls may start and finish in actual execution order, and approval display order never serializes handler execution. A projection that fails Floret validation or cannot be mapped is rejected as a unit and does not clear existing live content; a valid zero-segment projection clears the assistant blocks without inventing a body block. Canonical raw message projection requires exact nonempty thread, turn, run, message, role, status, and timestamp fields; every block must be a non-null supported JSON object. Bootstrap and `timeline.replaced` decode canonical arrays atomically, so one invalid row or block rejects the whole projection instead of partially rendering it. Stop and hard-cancel paths update current-process presentation but do not persist a canceled assistant row. Activity timeline changes enter the UI only inside Floret-derived projection activity segments delivered through `message.block_set`, a live draft, or a projection-backed timeline snapshot. Ordinary incremental events do not publish companion full timeline replacements. Every ordinary terminal turn and pending terminal settlement deletes the exact matching draft and publishes one `timeline.replaced` snapshot rebuilt from `ListThreadTurns`; an identity or ordinal mismatch requests resynchronization. `stream_generation` remains a Service-instance epoch so restart cannot let a stale high cursor hide new events.

Provider attempt activation is a presentation fence. `message.started` may carry
the Floret attempt epoch; an older epoch is ignored, while a higher epoch rebases
the same assistant draft onto the latest validated cumulative Floret turn
projection. Assistant text, Activity, and approval segments already present in
that projection form a stable canonical prefix. Redeven clears only block slots
after that prefix, assigns the next thinking or text block the first suffix
index, and never restarts block numbering at zero over canonical Activity. The
server and browser materializers retain the prefix when they apply
`message.started`; they do not infer tool retention from block content. The epoch
is an in-memory fence and is never used to replace canonical timeline or run
lifecycle authority.

Active cursor ownership belongs to Redeven's live projection. The projection marks at most one live assistant draft with `active_cursor` while the selected thread is running, and canceled, completed, idle, background, or merely streaming-shaped messages are not treated as active unless the projection marks them active. The visible model status affordance is a localized bottom dock lane driven by `model_io.updated`, not by `active_cursor` or thread running status. `model_io` is derived in memory from validated Floret provider lifecycle and stream observations: provider request maps to waiting for model response; assistant, reasoning, and model tool-call stream observations map to thinking; provider retry maps to retrying; provider finish maps to finalizing. Redeven does not persist Floret step, run, context-continuation, or compaction lifecycle mirrors. Provider diagnostics use typed finish fields; metadata cannot replace lifecycle facts.

Before Floret admission, Redeven may persist a command with only a stable `queue_id`, prompt, product resource references, launch options, and empty canonical turn/run fields. No user message or assistant draft is published from that command. The browser and server never generate TurnID or RunID. A queued response returns the exact `queue_id` once the command is durable. A start or request-user-input response waits until Floret's committed user-entry event is publicly readable, Redeven has atomically bound the canonical TurnID/RunID and settled command resources, and one admission `timeline.replaced` has been published. The in-memory completion signal carries the Floret-assigned identity and outcome. If presentation fails after canonical admission, the durable admission receipt remains authoritative while assistant presentation is blocked. A crash before admission leaves only Redeven-owned command state; a crash after admission is reconciled by the same LogicalRequestID plus exact Floret reads. Secret answers never enter plaintext persistence.

Flower may show one connection-local pending submission preview in the transcript while admission is unresolved, but that preview is not a message, has no canonical lifecycle authority, and is never inferred to be queued from thread status. Only an explicit queued receipt or canonical `queued_turns` membership places content in the composer-adjacent queue dock. Server `queued_turns` project as independent `queued_turn` entries keyed by `queue_id`, with prompt, attachments, linked context, and creation time; they are not messages and never enter canonical history. Explicit empty queued snapshots clear them, and a canonical Floret user row suppresses stale queued detail only after the durable admission receipt binds that queue to the exact TurnID. Duplicate prompts remain distinct. Flower never classifies queue membership by prompt, timestamp, position, assistant id, UserEntryID, pending request state, or thread run status, and it does not store a UI queue in local storage or another durable cache.

Selected-thread live delivery treats `model_io.updated` as a presentation boundary. Even when one live batch contains a short provider stream followed by finalizing or clearing events, Flower commits the model status lane and yields a render frame at each model I/O boundary. Desktop and Env App consume one cancellable fetch-SSE connection for the selected thread. A `ready` envelope advertises the current selected-thread and summary high-water marks; it does not acknowledge those sequences or advance either client cursor. Only a canonical bootstrap cursor or an event batch that the reducer successfully applies advances the corresponding cursor, so reconnect requests every retained event after the last applied position. Transport errors reconnect sequentially with bounded backoff, while generation changes, retention gaps, and slow-observer overflow request canonical resynchronization. The control flow distinguishes a user thread switch or hidden-page cancellation from network error, proxy closure, client parse failure, server resync, and retention gap: client transport failures remain silent and retryable, while server resync categories reload canonical bootstrap. None of these observer reasons creates a run error or the “Flower could not finish this reply” presentation; only canonical thread error authority may do so. Each SSE data frame and heartbeat receives a fresh bounded write deadline that is cleared after a successful flush, so an idle interval cannot expire the next heartbeat or reply write. Companion delivery stops while the document is hidden and restarts from its last applied cursor when visible. Cancellation releases the subscription, service shutdown and retirement close observers, and the retained event buffer remains the recovery source.

Summary and selected-thread detail cursor domains are independent. A
`summary.batch` may retain the originating thread event sequence for patch
identity, but applying it advances only `summary_after_seq`; it never consumes
that thread's detail replay. Only an applied `thread.batch` or canonical
bootstrap advances the selected thread cursor. Flower retains full detail for
at most eight recently used threads while keeping summary rows for the complete
list. Selecting a retained thread displays its in-memory snapshot immediately
and concurrently revalidates canonical bootstrap. Eviction strips messages,
approval/input detail, live model state, and that thread's detail cursor and
generation, but never composer text, attachments, reference selection, focus,
or scroll state. Selecting an evicted thread therefore waits for canonical
bootstrap instead of flashing stale detail. A terminal reply missed while an
unselected retained thread was open is still replaced by revalidation.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
Flower does not sort messages, infer canonical insertion points from timestamps or IDs, pair recent user messages with assistant drafts, promote a pending preview into canonical history, or reconcile queue rows by equal prompt text. `timeline.replaced` replaces the reducer message array in server order. A streaming assistant row requires exact canonical thread/turn/run/message identity; an unmatched draft triggers resynchronization and is never appended. Full thread detail and explicit summary patches own `queued_turns`, including an explicit empty list that clears queue-snapshot entries; omission does not impersonate that owned empty state. Once the canonical user row for the same TurnID appears, it wins over stale queued detail immediately in running, terminal, failed, or canceled state.

Flower does not rebuild Floret execution order from Redeven database rows, audit data, provider deltas, previews, or tool-call records. Floret `ListThreadTurns` is the durable message and ordering source; live runtime projections and pending settlement projections may update only the matching canonical turn. Flower does not scan cached block JSON or activity rows to repair pending, waiting, or running tool states after stop or approval. Redeven does not publish independent activity blocks from aggregate observations, synthesize final rows, hide queued siblings, or turn an invalid projection into an empty assistant block.

Redeven may publish `timeline.replaced` only at canonical user admission, explicit resync, snapshot recovery, or terminal settlement finalization. The admission replacement must precede provider, assistant, and tool presentation. Replacement is not a high-frequency companion for streaming text, block updates, run status changes, or ordinary thread patches. Desktop and Env App adapters both refresh the live bootstrap after thread-level stop operations, so the surface receives the same canonical timeline after a stop-only or stop+send interaction.

concepts.summary:
Redeven uses a shared Flower turn launcher for contextual Ask Flower entrypoints. The launcher is a focused first-turn composer: it previews the captured context, accepts one prompt, calls the shared turn-launch contract, and then lets the host surface hand off to the correct full Flower chat destination.

Floret remains authoritative after admission. Known pre-dispatch failures preserve the launcher draft for retry; uncertain post-dispatch outcomes hand off to the exact proposed thread and TurnID without resending; a later bootstrap failure remains a canonical-load error rather than permission to invent a transcript row or alternate admission path.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## Mechanism

Shared Flower contracts define `FlowerTurnLauncherIntent`, context items, attachments, and the shared `FlowerSurfaceAdapter` turn controls: `launchTurn` for admission and `stopThread` for canceling the selected running thread. `launchTurn` returns only a strict `FlowerTurnLaunchReceipt`: `admitting` carries the stable thread and admission identity while canonical projection is still converging, `start` carries the accepted thread/turn/run identity, and `queued` carries the durable Redeven queue identity. It never performs or returns the subsequent canonical bootstrap read. New and existing conversations both send through `POST /api/ai/threads/{thread_id}/turns`; a new conversation includes the strict creation snapshot in that same request, so settings intent, create operation, immutable first command, and attachment claim transfer freeze before Floret admission. The backend resolves that product-side frozen state before opening canonical read authority, establishes the canonical root through the Floret create coordinator, and then starts the exact frozen command. A repeated request reuses its original logical identity; exact canonical receipt verification occurs only after the create operation is committed. Desktop and Env App reject empty, HTML, or malformed JSON responses as typed uncertain outcomes instead of exposing a generic `invalid json` failure or retrying with another identity.

The full Flower composer owns no durable editable draft. One shell connection creates one in-memory draft coordinator shared by Activity, Workbench, the floating drawer, and surface remounts. Scope changes preserve the corresponding text, ordered references, attachments, and composer choices inside that connection. Another connection starts with independent memory, and no lease, takeover, conflict banner, recovery setting, host API, or browser persistence participates. Uploaded bytes may remain under a capability-bound staging scope, but that scope cannot restore editable text or references.

The launcher exposes `onSubmit` instead of owning host navigation, and its busy state blocks input, close, context, and duplicate submission until the callback settles. `FlowerSurface` uses the same `launchTurn` path for new and continued conversations, then refreshes canonical bootstrap independently after a receipt. Desktop Welcome submits from an environment card and opens its Flower page; Env App captures its view-mode target when opening and routes the receipt to Activity or Workbench without re-reading current mode. Gateway sessions preserve `runtime_gateway` as their execution source. A linked preview requires a runtime-valid `context_action`; an explicit malformed action is rejected rather than silently becoming a context-free turn.

Activity and Workbench both preserve the existing floating `FlowerTurnLauncherWindow`; Activity does not replace it with an inline panel. Exact focus routing and single-surface ownership are defined in [Flower Activity companion](flower-activity-companion.md). An ordinary Activity submit closes the launcher, preserves the active business surface, expands the fixed Flower work-detail overlay, and focuses the exact admitted or uncertain thread. A submit originating from the dedicated Flower page remains full-page and does not stack an overlay. Neither path changes the admission contract.

Ask Flower entrypoints deliberately separate linked context from file content sharing. File browser background/single/multi-selection menus, Codespaces directories, Activity and Workbench file previews, and future editor-preview launchers create `file_path` context items only; selecting text in a file preview does not create model-visible `file_selection` context and does not auto-create a pending text attachment. Terminal content and session menus create one `terminal_selection`. An explicit terminal selection has priority: short selected text remains inline, while long selections are linked by Unicode code-point length/truncation metadata only. Without a selection, the launcher reads the target Core's latest terminal screen through the released Floeterm terminal-info and buffer-line APIs, bounds oversized screen text to the most recent 10,000 Unicode code points with a visible leading omission marker, and includes that text inline. Terminal `working_dir` and `suggested_working_dir_abs` are optional: a verified local-path capability adds the same canonical absolute directory to both projections, while SSH, pending, failed, unknown, deleted, or otherwise unverified state omits both fields. Explicit empty or multiline fields remain invalid. An empty or unavailable screen still opens Ask Flower with metadata-only terminal context and a visible note, whether or not a verified directory exists; it does not create an invalid empty canonical reference. None of these paths creates an implicit file attachment. Monitoring process menus create `process_snapshot` metadata, Git Changes/branch/commit surfaces create bounded generated `text_snapshot` summaries, and Desktop Welcome creates environment metadata snapshots with the same fallback title used by the launcher. `editor_preview` remains a protocol-compatible file-path source without a producer.

Git browser launchers cover repository, workspace section and item, branch, branch status section and item, commit, stash, stash file, and branch-compare file targets. Every launcher captures the menu-open target and repository root before dispatch, bounds file lists and generated text, and emits only `text_snapshot` context. A launcher may fetch missing commit or stash detail before opening Flower, but changing environment, page mode, Git subview, or stash-window ownership cancels that pending launch. Git paths in the generated snapshot remain descriptive text; they do not become `file_path` grants or historical-file attachments.

Pending attachments remain an explicit launcher transport feature and are not converted into file-path linked context. Env App and Desktop create an exact target-thread staging scope, keep its plaintext capability only in connection memory, and send the scope id plus capability through fixed headers for upload, preview, deletion, release, and admission. A missing, repeated, expired, or mismatched capability fails closed. The backend converts each selected staged resource into a Floret canonical attachment containing only an opaque resource reference, name, MIME type, size, and optional text statistics. Before admission, static preflight verifies exact queued ownership, canonical metadata and digest shape, size, MIME, model capability, and provider route without opening current-schema file bytes. After canonical admission, the Floret prepared-request boundary opens and revalidates the exact bytes, size, and digest, then freezes the complete rendered payload, conservative estimate, and fingerprint before provider dispatch. Upload URLs, capability plaintext, and file bodies never enter JSON receipts, Floret journal metadata, or context-action events.

Flower does not create an optimistic canonical transcript message. After the full composer freezes an exact submission, it immediately moves the visible text into one product-owned, connection-memory pending preview, clears the visible composer, marks the composer busy, and disables duplicate submission. The preview uses a distinct pending-submission identity and dashed presentation with a localized sending status; it is never a `FlowerChatMessage`, carries no invented TurnID or message id, and does not enter timeline projection, thread persistence, read state, or live cursor ownership. Attachment names and linked-reference labels may remain visible as submission context, while attachment bytes and capabilities retain their existing transport boundaries.

A known failure before successful admission removes the preview and restores the exact composer draft. An uncertain post-dispatch outcome retains the preview and existing client request identity while the surface refreshes the exact reported thread; it never resends automatically. Once the uncertain handoff is returned to an exact thread, the frozen draft may remain available for an explicit idempotent retry with that same client request identity, but it is never assigned a new logical identity. A valid `kind=admitting`, `kind=start`, or `kind=queued` receipt moves the preview to an awaiting-projection phase and clears the accepted draft. Only an explicit queued receipt may move the preview into the queue dock; selected-thread `running`, SSE connectivity, composer busy state, and receipt latency never imply queue membership. The preview disappears when the corresponding canonical user projection or exact queue id is observed, so only the authoritative canonical message or `queued_turn` remains. Selecting another conversation, explicitly starting a new conversation, remounting, or reloading clears this in-memory presentation; recovery after that boundary comes only from canonical bootstrap or Redeven-owned `queued_turns`. A later bootstrap failure keeps the accepted preview visible as a projection error and does not restore a retryable draft.

A `kind=start` receipt is returned only after Floret has persisted the canonical user entry and Redeven has published the corresponding `timeline.replaced`; the surface independently refreshes bootstrap after receipt. A `kind=admitting` receipt exposes the already stable thread and admission identity before that canonical read boundary finishes. A `kind=queued` receipt means only that Redeven has durably stored an unadmitted command. Settings and model catalog reads are adapter-instance cached for five seconds with shared in-flight requests, invalidated by every settings mutation, and still revalidated by the server during admission. Handler resolution is warmed with the surface and shares one matching in-flight decision request with submission, so these product reads do not add duplicate work to the first visible turn.

Thread detail and live summary patches expose those Redeven-owned commands as `queued_turns`, allowing refresh, remount, Activity/Workbench handoff, and service restart to rebuild their prompt, TurnID, creation time, attachments, and linked context. Flower projects each one as a distinct `queued_turn` timeline entry, never as `FlowerChatMessage` or canonical history. The composer-adjacent queue dock is a compact, bounded projection of that same field: one stable single-line row per exact queue id, compact attachment/context metadata, reorder, send-now, and delete actions. Deleting calls the canonical followup service, hides only that exact row optimistically, and reloads canonical detail after success or failure. A conflict or not-found caused by concurrent promotion or reorder therefore converges to server state; failure restores the original canonical order and reports a nonblocking error. `queued_turns` is an owned detail field: omission in a partial summary preserves loaded detail, an explicit empty list clears queue-snapshot-owned rows, and a nonempty list replaces those rows. A canonical user row keeps its Floret `UserEntryID` as `message.id` and carries its owning Floret `TurnID` separately as `message.turn_id`. When bootstrap or `timeline.replaced` contains that exact TurnID, Flower renders only the canonical row even if stale queue detail still reports the command. Prompt content, timestamps, message ids, completion state, and entry-id collisions never participate in replacement. Redeven does not persist a TurnID-to-UserEntryID mapping; the relationship is projected directly from the current Floret turn snapshot.

Transcript linked-context actions distinguish host navigation from self-contained snapshot preview. In Env App, file chips delegate their canonical path to the existing live File Preview host and directory chips delegate to the existing Files host, so Activity, Workbench, and mobile placement remain owned by the standard environment controllers. The shared Flower floating preview accepts only text and process snapshot actions, including short terminal selections, historical display-only file selections, and generated Git or environment snapshots; it must never render a placeholder file or directory window. A host exposes file and directory navigation independently through optional adapter capabilities. Desktop Welcome does not expose those capabilities, so file and directory records from shared local history remain visible but noninteractive there. Capability absence and host failures never fall back to an explanatory or empty floating window.

Flower thread working directory is a Redeven product thread attribute decided at creation time. `FlowerSurfaceAdapter` exposes optional working-directory picker reads for path context and directory entries; Env App implements them through the existing runtime FS RPC, while Desktop Welcome implements them through the fixed runtime FS Local API bridge. In New chat, `FlowerSurface` keeps a local `workingDirDraft`, displays only the basename in the header chip, opens the shared `DirectoryPicker` when the chip is clicked, and sends `working_dir` only when creating a new thread. Existing threads display their immutable `thread.working_dir` basename with the full path in title/ARIA text; clicking that chip copies the full path and never opens a picker or patches the thread.

The full chat composer's working-directory `@` discovery, editable chips, strict `flower_composer` action, and ordered admission comparison are owned by [Flower composer references](flower-composer-references.md). They reuse `launchTurn` without changing the focused first-turn launcher's interaction contract.

Env App implements `stopThread` with the existing AI RPC stop endpoint and then reloads the thread bootstrap. Desktop implements the same adapter method through the runtime Flower HTTP bridge, which allows `POST /_redeven_proxy/api/ai/threads/:id/cancel` and reloads `/live/bootstrap`. The app server thread cancel route preserves RWX permission checks and audit events while calling `StopThread`. An active run is canceled and canonically finalized first; queued followups are recovered to drafts only after that terminal boundary, before the endpoint returns success.

Stop cancellation is canonical-terminal and engine-admission guarded. One caller budget covers exact-run cancellation, PTY/process settlement, the authority barrier, canonical verification, lifecycle locking, SubAgent closure, and queued-followup recovery; timeout returns pending while a service-owned finalizer continues. The per-thread finalization guard blocks a replacement run, is shared by concurrent Stop calls, and is removed only by compare-and-delete after the matching terminal snapshot is verified. Missing ownership, changed identity, or nonterminal canonical state returns unavailable; active-run maps, audit rows, broadcasts, threadstore records, and synthetic canceled state never substitute for Floret. Redeven-requested cancel and timeout project their canonical canceled/timed-out result rather than `floret_engine_failed`.

Environment cards can expose placement-shaped targets such as local container, SSH, provider, or Gateway targets. These identifiers are routing context for Redeven, not permission to infer Docker, SSH, systemd, or Gateway control commands. Flower must interpret environment lifecycle requests through the `redeven-environment` system skill and the `redeven env ... --json` surface so unsupported target kinds return structured product plans instead of lower-level command guesses. For arbitrary OS diagnostics on a selected target, the same skill routes Flower to `redeven targets exec --target <target> --command <agent-selected command> --json`, where Redeven owns target resolution and execution provenance.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body:
The launcher is not a persistent chat surface and does not inject drafts into the full Flower composer. Its visible text survives only inside its owning connection and component lifecycle. Hosts must not require a second send in the full chat, navigate ordinary Activity work to the dedicated Flower page, or re-read the current Env mode at submit time to decide the handoff target. A failure known to occur before admission dispatch, including an Env `ProtocolNotConnectedError`, or an explicit HTTP/RPC rejection envelope returned by the admission handler, clears the busy state, preserves the visible in-memory text, restores the ArrowUp action, presents the host error, and returns focus to the textarea.

An unknown ThreadID without `create` is a normal not-found and never enters initial-create recovery. A prepared create operation or frozen command may resume only when its settings snapshot, model, permission, text, ordered attachments, context action, options, session/channel, and create fingerprint match exactly. Missing canonical authority on an ordinary existing thread remains a canonical-load failure. These failures cannot be repaired by swallowing `ErrThreadNotFound`, resending with another identity, or rebuilding a Floret root from Redeven metadata.

Response loss after dispatch is an uncertain admission bound to the already proposed thread and logical request. A successful response with an invalid or mismatched receipt is also uncertain because the handler may already have admitted the turn. The full Flower surface retains its noncanonical pending preview while it refreshes the exact server thread and clears it only when canonical projection proves the outcome; it never automatically resends or classifies the preview as queued from thread status. Desktop Welcome and Env App close the external launcher and hand off to the exact thread without restoring a retryable launcher draft. This classification uses typed transport facts without status-text heuristics: Desktop IPC distinguishes an HTTP response, local pre-dispatch failure, and an unknown transport outcome; Env RPC distinguishes remote rejection, a detached call that was not sent, and RPC transport failure. The adapters never generate a second logical identity for that attempt. Once a valid receipt exists, a later bootstrap failure is a refresh failure rather than a send failure: the draft remains cleared, Flower exposes the canonical-load error, and the existing live-resync path remains authoritative without a canonical synthetic row or resubmission. The launcher adds no artificial minimum loading delay, timer, local storage queue, or fallback lifecycle state.

Runtime admission may queue a turn submitted while another run remains active. Redeven must not read Floret sqlite, synthesize Floret tool results from audit rows, or treat terminal audit cancellation as a substitute for Floret durable tool-call/tool-result closure. `waiting_user` threads stay on the structured input Continue flow and do not enter ordinary turn admission; their admission response must still contain nonempty TurnID and RunID with exact `kind=start` before the adapter reloads bootstrap. Focus handoff is a consumed request, not persistent selected-thread state; after `FlowerSurface` accepts a request or the user selects another thread, the host clears that request so remounts and list refreshes cannot pull the user back to the handoff thread. Thread working directories are not mutable after creation: appserver thread patch decoding rejects unknown fields such as `working_dir`, and an empty create request falls back to the runtime `agentHomeDir` before validation. Context actions are product records rather than UI-only metadata: the runtime validates the standard Ask Flower action before accepting the turn, persists the normalized envelope only while the command is queued, and projects the accepted record into Floret only as current-turn supplemental context. File-related context is path/metadata-only, and upload URLs or file bodies must not be displayed as implied model context in launcher copy. The target context does not alter builtin tool execution. In particular, `terminal.exec` still runs in the local AI runtime; only Redeven product command results or target-routed tool results with explicit `execution_location` can justify saying a command ran on a selected target. Queued context-action JSON is validated strictly; damaged queue data is an error and is never repaired into executable input.

A persisted file path is display and navigation metadata, not a filesystem read grant. After a user click, the Env App host normalizes the path and delegates to its existing preview or directory surface, where session and filesystem read policy remains authoritative. That host read does not mutate the context action, attach file contents to the transcript, or create new model-visible supplemental context. Desktop and any future host without the matching capability must render the reference without a click affordance instead of inventing a fallback interaction.

Git menu navigation and inspection actions are separate from the captured Flower context. Terminal and Files handoffs use the effective live repository or worktree directory. `Preview Current File` opens only the current filesystem file at the resolved path, including the destination path for renamed or copied entries; it is unavailable for deleted entries and never represents a commit or stash snapshot. Historical diff remains owned by the existing Git diff source contract.

concepts.title: Git browser visual states
concepts.description: Keep Git selection, repository facts, semantic status, hover, and focus visually independent across themes.

frontmatter.description: Keep Git selection, repository facts, semantic status, hover, and focus visually independent across themes.
frontmatter.title: Git browser visual states

concepts.summary: Env App's Git browser uses each Floe theme's native selection and focus roles for selected navigation and rows, while Classic Light retains Redeven's established blue interaction system and Git status colors remain reserved for repository meaning. The currently checked-out branch is a repository fact and the selected branch is the user's inspection target; either may exist without the other, and both remain visible when they coincide. Hover and keyboard focus provide separate transient feedback. If a theme cannot preserve these distinctions and readable text, the visual contract fails rather than falling back to an unrelated fixed palette or ambiguous neutral styling.

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
## State ownership

Selected navigation, branch rows, history rows, status summaries, and changed-file rows share the Git selection accent, background, border, and indicator tokens. List-like selections use a filled surface plus a solid left indicator. Segmented tabs keep their contained active-item presentation and do not adopt list indicators. Hover uses a lower-emphasis neutral surface and never overrides an active selection. Keyboard focus uses a distinct outline that remains visible on selected and unselected controls.

The Current branch chip is independent of selection styling. It always uses the current-branch chip tokens, including when the current branch is selected. Git change and health tones such as success, warning, danger, info, and remote-branch violet remain on semantic icons, badges, paths, and values; they must not determine a selection indicator or focus ring.

## Theme and accessibility

Every built-in light and dark shell preset inherits the complete Git interaction token set. Themes, including Classic Dark, derive selected surfaces from Floe's published `selection-bg` and derive selection indicators and focus rings from the theme `ring`, with a small foreground mixture in dark themes where needed to preserve adjacent-color contrast. This keeps warm, green, violet, neutral, and blue themes within their own interaction identity. Light themes use a restrained selection mixture over the panel; dark themes use a stronger mixture so selection does not disappear into dark panels, while Classic Dark keeps a quieter surface mixture suited to its elevated panels. Classic Light explicitly retains Redeven's validated blue roles. Selected text and current-chip text meet a 4.5:1 contrast target. Selection indicators and focus rings meet a 3:1 adjacent-color target, while selected, hover, and idle surfaces retain measurable perceptual separation. Forced-colors mode exposes selected borders, indicators, focus outlines, and current-chip boundaries through system colors.

sections.title: Boundaries
sections.body: This contract changes presentation only. It does not alter Git state, selection ownership, keyboard navigation, ARIA state, workspace generation, or Files decoration. Product themes may vary selection hue and surrounding surfaces, but they must not replace interaction roles with Git semantic status colors, inherit a fixed palette from another theme, or make Current a proxy for selection.
